root.name: French Defense: Orthoschnapp Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. c4 d5 3. cxd5 exd5 4. Qb3

overview: After the exchange on d5, White's 4.Qb3 hits d5 and b7 and invites 4...dxe4, offering a pawn for activity. Black can also defend with 4...Nf6 or 4...Be6 and reach a normal exchange-type position with White's queen out early. I am not sure which reply is main; the gambit pawn on e4 can be kept by Black with careful play.

white_ideas.idea: Use the queen on b3 to pressure d5 and b7 and develop Nc3, Nf3 and Bb5+ quickly.
Regain the e4 pawn with Nc3 and Bb5+ if Black takes it.

black_ideas.idea: Defend d5 with ...Nf6 or ...Be6 and develop calmly.
Accept with ...dxe4 and return the pawn when needed to complete development.

typical_structures.structure: Black pawn on d5 with an open e-file after trades, or Black a pawn up after ...dxe4.

character.notes: Queen-led early play with open lines; risks on both sides but not clearly attacking.

gambit.notes: If Black captures with 4...dxe4 the pawn is not regained by force.

soundness.notes: Early queen sortie for a pawn; not enough compensation against accurate play.

structure.notes: Pawns exchanged in the centre leaves open lines.

approach.notes: Strong players rarely choose it; mostly a surprise.

level.notes: Dubious, so not Beginner; plans are simple.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4...Nf6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. c4 d5 3. cxd5 exd5 4. Qb3 Nf6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black declines the gambit; no material changes hands.

character.reason: An early queen and a pawn gambit with open lines.

gambit.reason: White offers the e4 pawn which Black can keep.

soundness.reason: An early queen sortie for thin compensation.

structure.reason: Central pawns are exchanged, leaving open lines.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom meet the French with this line.

plans.reason: White's queen comes out early to speed development.
